thread:
sam: Quick sync — we need a safer per-tenant canary UX for Dedicated customers. Current console only supports a single percent slider and operators are unsure how that maps to actual RPS/reserved capacity.

maria: +1. Hit this with Acme yesterday — they bumped to 20% and immediately hit their quota because 20% -> very bursty traffic. We need both percent and an absolute cap view. :grimacing:

jordan: Can we show an estimated RPS and a projected cost delta in the rollout modal? Operator wants to see "what does 20% mean in my tenant units" before confirming.

akiko: Agree. Also need clear guards: automated rollback if error_rate > 5% or p95 latency regresses by >30% for N=5m. Otherwise ops will manually revert too late.

tess: Quick question: should rollback be based on relative change vs baseline or absolute thresholds? For low-traffic tenants relative noise kills canaries.

maria: For Dedicated enterprise tenants we should support a safety_matrix that supports both: {"min_reqs": 50, "error_rate_pct_delta": 200, "abs_error_rate": 3}. If requests < min_reqs, don't auto-rollback on pct changes, rely on abs threshold.

sam: I like that. UX needs to surface the safety matrix and an "operational impact" score. Idea: show red/yellow/green with a short reason line (e.g., "auto-rollback: enabled — will trigger if abs_errors > 3% or p95 latency > 1200ms").

leo: Implementation notes: backend already emits per-tenant SLIs (error_rate, lat_p95, qps). We need to (1) compute rolling deltas vs baseline, (2) publish a canary decision event to the orchestration layer, (3) track the canary lifecycle in telemetry.

jordan: Also want an operator override: a "pause" that sets canary traffic to 0% instantly (instead of waiting for gradual ramp-down). That must be audited with who/when.

akiko: +1 on audit. Also add a safer default ramp: [1%, 5%, 10%, 25%] with per-step hold time computed from baseline RPS (hold = max(120s, 10x inter-arrival-sample)). Means high-qps tenants will progress faster, but low-qps tenants get longer holds for signal.

maria: UX mock: show two controls side-by-side — "Percent of tenant traffic" slider AND "Absolute RPS cap" input. The slider adjusts the cap preview. If cap < autoscale_min, we display a warning.

sam: We also need to define fallback behavior if a Dedicated tenant exceeds their reserved capacity during a canary: do we queue, reject (429), or divert to shared pool? Current behavior is inconsistent.

leo: For Enterprise we should default to divert->shared pool with a circuit-breaker: once diverted > 10% of canary window, auto-pause canary and notify tenant. For strict isolation customers we should reject with 429. That should be per-tenant policy.

tess: That means the rollout API must accept a policy flag: "overflow_handler": ["reject","divert","throttle"], plus a "soft_quota_threshold" percent to start diverting earlier.

maria: Example rollout config (proto-ish):
```yaml
canary:
  steps: [1,5,10,25]
  step_hold_seconds: null # server computes based on traffic
  safety_matrix:
    min_reqs: 50
    abs_error_rate_pct: 3
    error_rate_pct_delta: 200
    p95_latency_ms_delta_pct: 30
  overflow_handler: divert
  overflow_divert_policy:
    target: shared_pool
    divert_pct_start: 90
    auto_pause_threshold_pct: 10
```

jordan: Love that. One API UX debate: expose percents as floats (12.5%) or integers with basis points? Float is friendlier in console, but basis points are safer for invariants. Thoughts?

akiko: For console show floats, API store integer basis points internally. Conversion is trivial.

sam: Telemetry requirements: emit canary.progress events with {step, duration, metrics_snapshot, decision} and link to trace IDs. Those should feed the dashboard so ops can see "why" a step passed/failed.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary policy changes require schema bump v2.1.0 and a migration for existing rollouts that used the old percent-only model.

maria: Migration plan — keep old canaries working by computing a default safety_matrix from tenant profile and set overflow_handler=divert by default for non-isolated tenants. For isolated tenants prompt an ops migration (manual).

sam: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with UX mock and API sketch. @maria can you prototype the modal mock? @leo can you outline the telemetry events? I'll capture the policy flags and we can sync Wed 9am.

maria: On it, I'll post a gif mock tomorrow. :+1:

jordan: I'll follow up on cost-estimation bits (projected tokens/cost delta) and add to RFC.

akiko: I'll draft rollback rules for the safety_matrix and share test harness to simulate low/high qps canaries.

sam: Thanks all. If anyone sees major gaps reply here, otherwise I'll open the RFC.
